insider_note: Two halves: what it is, and how it is made. The second half needs BOTH enzymes — the same restriction enzyme cuts both DNAs so the sticky ends match, and DNA ligase joins them.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Recombinant DNA defined
steps.margin_note: Definition naming both sources. Four lines.
lines: RECOMBINANT DNA is a HYBRID DNA molecule
formed by joining a desired gene from one organism to
It contains DNA from two different sources.
steps.why: The molecule is called recombinant because it combines DNA that was never together in nature.
common_mistakes: Saying recombinant DNA is a mutated DNA. It is a JOINED molecule, not a changed one.
Leaving out the two sources. That is what makes it recombinant.
steps.memory_tip: Two DNAs from two organisms, joined into one.

steps.label: How it is made
steps.margin_note: Both enzymes, and the same-enzyme point. Five lines.

lines.text: Restriction enzyme cuts, DNA ligase joins

lines: Both DNAs are cut with the SAME restriction
enzyme, so their sticky ends match.
The enzyme DNA LIGASE then joins them by covalent
The product is the recombinant DNA.
steps.why: The same enzyme on both molecules is what makes the ends complementary, and ligase seals what the sticky ends have already brought together.
common_mistakes: Naming only one enzyme. BOTH the restriction enzyme and ligase are needed.
Saying different enzymes are used on the two DNAs. The SAME one must be used.
steps.memory_tip: One enzyme to cut both, one to join them.
